name: Instructional Design and Educational Technology
description: Designing how people learn — analysing needs, building courses and materials, choosing and evaluating technology, and measuring whether any of it worked. ⚠⚠⚠ In Florida it is a graduate field and almost nothing else: across the two CIP codes, public institutions awarded 978 credentials in 2023 and just SIX of them were bachelor's degrees. ⚠⚠ Which is why the undergraduate major question is genuinely open — you cannot major in this.
degreesNote: ⚠⚠⚠ SIX BACHELOR'S DEGREES IN THE ENTIRE STATE SYSTEM. Curriculum and Instruction (13.0301) produced 762 credentials at 10 Florida public institutions — 480 master's, 127 research doctorates, 67 postbaccalaureate certificates, 66 post-master's certificates, 22 professional doctorates, and NO bachelor's at all. Educational/Instructional Technology (13.0501) added 216 at 6 institutions — 162 master's, 27 postbaccalaureate certificates, 21 research doctorates and six bachelor's. ⚠ So this is a master's and certificate field, entered after some other degree, and that is the normal route rather than a compromise. ⚠⚠ THE POSTBACCALAUREATE CERTIFICATES ARE WORTH NOTICING: 94 across the two codes. They are the short route for someone already holding a degree and working — a teacher, a trainer, a subject expert — and they are much cheaper than the master's. Ask what a certificate qualifies you for in the sector you want, because the answer differs sharply between higher education and corporate work. ⚠⚠⚠ AND CHECK WHICH SECTOR THE PROGRAMME SERVES. Florida's programmes sit in colleges of education and are built around schools and universities. The larger and faster-growing employment is CORPORATE learning and development, where the federal occupation is Training and Development Specialists — 452,300 jobs against instructional coordinators' 232,600, and 78% of employers reporting a bachelor's as the entry requirement rather than a master's. ⚠ A degree aimed at the education sector is not wasted in industry, but it is not what industry screens on, which is a portfolio.

cips.note: Curriculum and Instruction — 10 Florida public institutions and 762 credentials in 2023: 480 master's, 127 research doctorates, 67 postbaccalaureate certificates, 66 post-master's certificates, 22 professional doctorates, ⚠ and zero bachelor's. Florida State 200, University of Florida 169, UWF 96, FIU 92, USF 87.

Educational/Instructional Technology — 6 Florida public institutions and 216 credentials: 162 master's, 27 postbaccalaureate certificates, 21 research doctorates and ⚠ just 6 bachelor's, the only undergraduate output in the field. Florida State 75, UCF 66, USF 29, UWF 20, FAU 18, UNF 8.

related.note: ⚠⚠ The commonest feeder by a long way — these programmes sit in colleges of education and are built around teachers moving into design, coaching and curriculum roles. ⚠ EME2040 Introduction to Technology for Educators is carried by 33 Florida public institutions, more than any other course in the prefix, and almost every Florida teaching student takes it.

⚠⚠⚠ Named because the LARGER employer is corporate, not educational. Training and development specialists number 452,300 nationally against 232,600 instructional coordinators, grow much faster, and 78% of employers report a bachelor's rather than a master's as the entry requirement. ⚠ A business or communication background plus a portfolio competes perfectly well there.

⚠ Named for the production half of the work: authoring tools, web delivery, video, accessibility and learning analytics. ⚠⚠ Florida's graduate curriculum reflects it — EME6405 Educational Web Design, EME6209 Digital Video, EME6208 Interactive Media — and a technical background is a genuine advantage in a field with no required major.

⚠ The discipline the field came out of: instructional design has its roots in applied learning psychology, and learning theory is the part that distinguishes a designer from a content producer. ⚠⚠ Psychology is taught at 33 Florida public institutions against this field's 10, so it is a far more available undergraduate starting point.

⚠ Named only because both sit in colleges of education and students confuse the departments. They are unrelated work: counselling is licensed clinical or school practice, instructional design is unlicensed and portfolio-driven.
